errors.current: khammana has a doubled middle letter, so its present forms start with u: ukhammin (I guess), yukhammin (he guesses), not akhammin.
errors.problem: The rule is wrong as stated. A doubled middle letter does not make the present start with u: Form V verbs also double the middle letter and start with a, e.g. تَصَفَّحَ → سَأَتَصَفَّحُ (in this same lesson, dialogue.lines[14]) and تَكَلَّمَ → أَتَكَلَّمُ. The u-prefix comes from the pattern: khammana is Form II (faʿʿala), and Form II presents start with u. A learner who follows the rule as written will say *utakallamu, *utaṣaffaḥu.
errors.fix: khammana is a Form II verb (pattern faʿʿala), and Form II presents start with u: ukhamminu (I guess), yukhamminu (he guesses), not akhamminu.

notes.note: The card still marks أَتَشَرَّفُ أَنْ أَتَقَدَّمَ as 'wrong', and Karim still says نَسْتَعْمِلُ دَائِمًا «بِأَنْ». Dropping bi- before an is regular and common in real letters; bi-an is the preferred formal choice, not the only correct one. Consider 'usually' and a softer card.
'istamaʿa always needs ilā': it also takes li- (اِسْتَمَعَ لَهُ). 'needs a preposition, usually ilā' would be safer.
أُعْلِنَ النَّتَائِجُ is marked wrong ('plurals of things take the feminine'). A verb before a broken plural may be masculine or feminine; the feminine is the preferred norm. Consider 'usually take'.
'It's the second-to-last week of the course' contradicts day 85 ('the last week of the course'); day 88 is in week 13, the final week.
وَنَصَحَهُمْ follows the sentence about Sami, so in Arabic it reads as 'Sami advised them'; the English says 'He' meaning Mr Karim. وَنَصَحَهُمُ الْأُسْتَاذُ would remove the ambiguity.
'ninety (-a after anna)': after anna the number takes its -īna form; the ending is not a plain -a. 'ninety (-īna after anna)' would be clearer.
«يَعْنِي» وَ«كَيْفَ أَقُولُ» تُعْطِيكَ: with two coordinated items the dual تُعْطِيَانِكَ is more careful; the feminine singular is tolerable.

summary: Read the whole days-81-90 export (3123 lines: days 81-90 sentences, mistake cards, dialogues, readings, quizzes, intros and culture notes) and checked the source for day 86. Arabic strings checked: 610 vocalised lines (plus their segs); 0 wrong in the Arabic itself: the passive (buniya/kutiba/uktushifa/yuqālu/tuṭfaʾu), conditionals with idhā/in/law and fa-, inna/anna/lākinna, kāna/ṣāra, numbers and ordinals, the formal-letter formulas and the round-2 fixes (اِكْتَشَفَ gloss, أَيُّ الْحُرُوفِ, الْمُشْكِلَةَ الْكُبْرَى, تُكَرِّرَ gloss, الْوَاحِدَةِ, هٰذِهِ, مِنْ gloss) are correct. Tap glosses checked: 1224 (in 383 tap lines) plus 3543 seg glosses; wrong: 24 tap glosses across 11 findings. Errors: 14 (1 major, 13 minor). The one major error is a wrong rule in the day-86 mistake card (a doubled middle letter does not make the present start with u; Form V tasaffaḥa/takallama contradicts it in the same lesson). One minor grammar-fact: the day-89 intro groups 'after kāna' with inna as taking -a. Most findings are round-2 tap-gloss findings that are still present (عَشَرَ 'twelfth' on 18th/19th, the second نَاحِيَةٍ glossed 'on the one hand', عُنْوَان 'address' on headline day, مَقَالَة, عَلَامَات, الْخَطّ, بَرِيدِيَّةً 'postcards', مِنُ, مُدِير '(of)'), plus الَّذِي glossed only 'who' in a gender-choice quiz, and one engine issue with bare letters in prose.
